statements.look-back-time: Light from a distant galaxy has been on its way for as many years as the galaxy is light years away, so the farther we look, the older the universe we see.
statements.cosmological-red-shift: The cosmological red shift is the stretching of the wavelength of light by the expansion of space while the light travels. Nearly every galaxy shows a red shift proportional to its distance; it is not a Doppler shift, and every observer sees the other galaxies receding.
statements.hubble-law: The recession velocity of a galaxy is proportional to its distance, $v = H_{0}d$, where the constant of proportionality $H_{0}$ is the Hubble constant.
statements.recession-speed-and-distance: Hubble's law turns a galaxy's distance into its recession speed and a recession speed, measured from a red shift, into a distance. The same arithmetic gives a rough age of the universe.
statements.cosmic-microwave-background: The cosmic microwave background is blackbody radiation at about 2.7 K that fills all of space, the remnant of the hot early universe stretched to long wavelengths by its expansion. Its discovery is the second great piece of evidence for the Big Bang.
statements.matter-antimatter-asymmetry: The universe is nearly pure matter, although particle physics is almost symmetric between matter and antimatter. A tiny asymmetry of the forces in the early universe left a little matter over when the rest annihilated.
statements.cmbr-wrinkles: The cosmic microwave background shows tiny variations, or wrinkles, from one direction to another. Galaxies could not have formed without such early fluctuations in density, and yet the background is so smooth that its smoothness needs an explanation.
statements.gravity-bends-light: Light has no mass, yet its path bends in a gravitational field, because mass curves space and light follows the curve. Its observation in the 1919 eclipse was the first verification of general relativity.
statements.gravitational-lensing: Gravitational lensing is the bending of light from a distant galaxy by the gravity of a nearer one, which acts like a converging lens and can form several images. It is a large-scale test of general relativity.
statements.schwarzschild-radius: The radius of the event horizon of a black hole is $R_{\text{S}} = 2GM/c^{2}$, in proportion to its mass. Since $G$ is small and $c^{2}$ is large, a black hole of a few solar masses is only a few kilometers across.
statements.find-schwarzschild-radius: The Schwarzschild radius $R_{\text{S}} = 2GM/c^{2}$ turns the mass of a black hole into the size of its event horizon, from a stellar black hole to a supermassive one at a galaxy's core.
statements.gravitational-waves: Gravitational waves are ripples in the curvature of space itself, sent out by moving masses as a water bug's foot sends waves across a pond. They travel at the speed of light and only extreme events make them strong enough to detect.
statements.flat-rotation-curve: The orbital speed of the stars in a galaxy stays almost constant out to great distances from its center, instead of falling off as it would if the galaxy's mass were concentrated, like its luminous stars, near the center. This flat rotation curve is the first evidence for dark matter.
statements.dark-matter: Dark matter is matter that cannot be seen but whose gravity shows it is there; there is about ten times as much of it in the universe as there is luminous matter, and what it is remains unknown.
statements.critical-density: The critical density $\rho_{\text{c}} \approx 10^{-26}\;\text{kg/m}^{3}$ is the average density of the universe that would just halt its expansion in a universe with no cosmological constant, a few nucleons per cubic meter.
statements.open-closed-flat-universe: An open universe is negatively curved and expands forever, a closed one is positively curved and returns a traveler to the start, and a flat one lies between. Measurements show the universe is very close to flat.
statements.machos-and-microlensing: MACHOs, small dark bodies in a galaxy's halo, would not block a star's light but would focus it as they pass in front of it, and the star would brighten in a characteristic manner. Searches for such microlensing test whether dark matter is ordinary matter.
statements.neutrino-oscillations: A neutrino can change from one flavor to another only if it has mass, since a massless neutrino travels at the speed of light and no time passes for it. Oscillations explain the missing solar neutrinos and could supply some of the dark matter.
statements.wimps: WIMPs are proposed weakly interacting massive particles, chargeless and of a completely new kind, that could make up dark matter. They would gather in halos rather than coalesce into spirals.
statements.complexity: Complexity is the study of complex adaptive systems, those that obey the simple laws of physics yet can adapt, organize themselves and evolve.
statements.chaos: Chaos is a system's extreme sensitivity to its initial conditions, so that a small change in where it starts changes its outcome tremendously and its long-term behavior cannot be predicted with precision.
statements.high-temperature-superconductors: High-temperature superconductors are ceramics, found since 1986, that superconduct above 77 K, the boiling point of cheap liquid nitrogen, which makes them economically interesting.
statements.superconductor-cooling-cost: A superconducting wire pays only when cooling it costs less than the energy a normal wire loses to heat, a comparison made with the power dissipated in a resistance and the price of electric energy.
statements.questions-at-every-scale: The open questions of physics lie on three scales, the largest, the intermediate and the smallest, and each rests on physics already known.

new.name: Cosmology
new.statement: Cosmology is the study of the character and evolution of the universe.

new.name: The Big Bang
new.statement: The Big Bang is the hot, dense beginning from which the universe has been expanding ever since, about 14 billion years ago.

new.name: The Hubble constant $H_{0}$
new.statement: The Hubble constant $H_{0}$ is the ratio of a galaxy's recession velocity to its distance, the slope of a graph of one against the other, about 20 (km/s)/Mly.

new.name: Superforce
new.statement: The superforce is the single unified force that the four basic forces are thought to have been at the highest energies of the early universe.

new.name: TOE epoch
new.statement: The TOE epoch is the time before about $10^{-43}$ s after the Big Bang, when all four forces were unified in the superforce.

new.name: GUT epoch
new.statement: The GUT epoch is the time after gravity separated, when the strong, weak and electromagnetic forces were still unified, ending about $10^{-35}$ s after the Big Bang.

new.name: Electroweak epoch
new.statement: The electroweak epoch is the time after the strong force separated, when the weak and electromagnetic forces were still unified, ending about $10^{-11}$ s after the Big Bang.

new.name: Spontaneous symmetry breaking
new.statement: Spontaneous symmetry breaking is the separation of a unified force into distinct forces as the universe cools, a transition that releases energy, as water releases energy when it freezes.

new.name: The inflationary scenario
new.statement: The inflationary scenario holds that the energy released when the strong force separated from the electroweak force expanded the universe by a factor of $10^{50}$ or more in an instant, stretching the early wrinkles nearly flat.

new.name: General relativity
new.statement: General relativity is Einstein's theory of gravitation, in which mass curves space and time and the curvature governs the motion of matter and light.

new.name: Thought experiment
new.statement: A thought experiment is an experiment carried out in the mind rather than with apparatus, to reason out what a theory implies.

new.name: Escape velocity
new.statement: The escape velocity of a body is the smallest speed an object must have at its surface to escape the body's gravity entirely.

new.name: Black hole
new.statement: A black hole is an object so dense that its escape velocity exceeds the speed of light, so that nothing, not even light, can escape from it.

new.name: Event horizon
new.statement: The event horizon is the distance from a black hole at which the escape velocity equals the speed of light; nothing inside it can get out.

new.name: Quasar
new.statement: A quasar is an extremely distant and luminous object, thought to be the center of a young galaxy powered by a supermassive black hole.

new.name: Quantum gravity
new.statement: Quantum gravity is the theory, not yet found, that would describe gravity where it is strong enough to act on the quantum scale, by joining quantum mechanics and general relativity.

new.name: Cosmological constant
new.statement: The cosmological constant is a term in Einstein's equations of general relativity that acts as a repulsion causing the expansion of the universe to accelerate.

new.name: Negatively curved universe
new.statement: A negatively curved universe is an open one, curved like a saddle, in which the angles of a large triangle add to less than $180^{\circ}$ and the expansion continues forever.

new.name: Positively curved universe
new.statement: A positively curved universe is a closed one, curved like a sphere, in which the angles of a large triangle add to more than $180^{\circ}$ and a traveler going straight returns to the start.

new.name: Flat universe
new.statement: A flat universe has zero curvature, so that the angles of a triangle add to exactly $180^{\circ}$; it lies between an open and a closed universe.

new.name: MACHOs
new.statement: MACHOs, massive compact halo objects, are dark bodies of ordinary matter, such as faint stars and planets, in a galaxy's halo, proposed as part of the dark matter.

new.name: Microlensing
new.statement: Microlensing is the brightening of a distant star when a small dark body passes in front of it and focuses its light by gravitational lensing.

new.name: Axions
new.statement: Axions are a proposed kind of light, weakly interacting particle that could make up some of the dark matter.

new.name: Neutralinos
new.statement: Neutralinos are proposed neutral, weakly interacting massive particles predicted by some theories, candidates for the dark matter.

new.name: Critical temperature $T_{\text{c}}$
new.statement: The critical temperature $T_{\text{c}}$ of a superconductor is the temperature at and below which it has zero resistivity.
